market_context: United States; commercially washed shell eggs sold under refrigeration
title: Should eggs be refrigerated?

seo.title: Should eggs be refrigerated? U.S. egg storage explained
seo.meta_description: Yes. In the U.S., commercially sold shell eggs should stay refrigerated at 40°F (4°C) or below because they are washed and sold under a cold chain.
seo.search_intent: Understand why U.S. eggs need refrigeration, how to store them, and why advice differs from some European countries.

excerpt: Yes. In the United States, commercially sold shell eggs should be refrigerated promptly at 40°F (4°C) or below and kept cold until use. U.S. eggs are commercially washed and normally sold under refrigeration, so taking them home and storing them on the counter breaks the cold chain. Keep them in the original carton on an interior shelf rather than repeatedly moving them between warm and cold temperatures.
content_html:
In a U.S. grocery store, eggs are normally in a refrigerated case. That is not just a merchandising choice. Commercial shell eggs in the United States should remain refrigerated after purchase at 40°F (4°C) or below.

The advice can look confusing if you have traveled in Europe, where eggs are often sold at room temperature. The difference comes largely from how eggs are processed and how the supply chain manages temperature.

U.S. eggs are washed and kept in a cold chain

Commercial egg processing in the United States includes washing and sanitizing the shell. Washing helps remove surface contamination, but it also changes the shell's natural protective coating. After processing, refrigeration becomes an important part of controlling bacterial growth.

That is why FDA guidance tells consumers to buy eggs only from a refrigerated case and put them promptly into a refrigerator at 40°F or below.

Once they are cold, keep them cold

A refrigerated egg should not spend hours warming on the counter and then return to the fridge. Warming can create condensation on the shell, and extended time at room temperature gives bacteria more opportunity to multiply.

FDA's general rule for refrigerated perishables is no more than two hours at room temperature, or one hour when the air temperature is above 90°F (32°C).

Store the carton on an interior shelf

The refrigerator door experiences repeated temperature swings every time it opens. An interior shelf stays more consistent. Keeping eggs in their original carton also protects them from breakage and strong odors and keeps the date information attached to the eggs.

A refrigerator thermometer is useful because the dial setting does not always tell you the actual food temperature.

How long can raw shell eggs stay refrigerated?

FDA recommends using shell eggs within about three weeks for best quality. Other U.S. storage charts may give a slightly longer refrigerated window, but the carton date and how the eggs have been handled still matter.

Quality changes over time even when eggs remain safe: the air cell grows, the white becomes thinner, and the yolk membrane weakens.

Do not wash eggs again at home

Commercial eggs have already been washed before sale. Rewashing them in the sink is unnecessary and can splash microorganisms around the kitchen.

Discard eggs with cracked shells unless the crack happened during your own handling and the egg is immediately transferred to a clean container and cooked thoroughly.

Why is European advice different?

Many European systems do not wash Grade A table eggs before retail and focus on avoiding temperature fluctuations and condensation before sale. That is why eggs can appear on unrefrigerated shelves there.

It does not mean Salmonella behaves differently in Europe or that U.S. eggs can safely copy the same storage pattern. Follow the storage system used where the eggs were produced and sold.

The practical rule

For eggs bought in the United States: buy them cold, take them home promptly, refrigerate at 40°F or below, and keep them cold until you are ready to cook them.

The grocery store and home refrigerator should be one continuous cold chain, not two separate storage methods.

faq.question: Can U.S. eggs be left on the counter?
faq.answer: Commercially refrigerated eggs should not be stored on the counter. FDA's general two-hour limit for refrigerated perishables applies, shortened to one hour above 90°F.

faq.question: Where should eggs go in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: Keep them in their original carton on an interior shelf where temperature is more stable than in the door.

faq.question: Why are eggs not refrigerated in some European stores?
faq.answer: Processing and temperature-management systems differ. Many European table eggs are not washed before retail and are kept at a relatively constant temperature to avoid condensation.
